newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian airline Tarom says to renew fleet.
newsitem.headline: Romanian airline Tarom says to renew fleet.

text.p: Romania's state airline Tarom SA denied on Monday reports in the local press saying the company had given up plans to renew its ageing fleet.
"Everything is on the right track as far as Tarom is concerned. We will go ahead with the plans to buy new aircraft," Tarom spokeswoman Rodica Balaci told Reuters.

On Monday, the daily newspaper Romania Libera quoted Tarom sources as saying the airline had suspended a plan to buy eight new Boeing 737s -- part of a project to upgrade Tarom's fleet -- following the Finance Ministry's alleged failure to issue a letter of credit needed to buy the new aircraft.
"There was indeed a May 20 deadline for that letter, which was not observed by the Finance Ministry. But this is not Tarom's problem," Balaci said.
Finance Ministry officials were unavailable for comment.

Tarom's international network, which includes most cities in western Europe plus U.S. flights, operates with a fleet of Soviet-made Tupolevs and Antonovs and Romanian-made British Aerospace Plc BAC 1-11s. It also has a number of newer Airbus and Boeing aircraft.

Under its latest restructuring programme, headed by aircraft purchases, Tarom is in the market for a replacement for its two Airbus 310s, possibly with McDonnell Douglas MD-11s Combi. It also plans to buy eight Boeing Next Generation 737s and seven ATR-42s, to replace its Soviet-made Antonov 24s.
In 1995, Tarom suffered a heavy blow when one of its Airbus 310's crashed after takeoff, killing all 59 on board.
The airline faces competition on domestic flights and on some regional flights from private companies as the Romanian-American joint venture JARO or the DAC Air airline.
